experiment: Matched Z–ZZ retraining verification and scalar MIA
structural_scope: 7 preselected matched Z–ZZ pairs × 2 encoders × 3 target-model seeds; complete all 42 target runs, including 6 missing MNIST runs.
experimental_unit: For target utility: one independently trained target model. For the encoder contrast: one matched pair × target-model seed, with Z and ZZ kept paired.
target_model_seeds: 3 model-initialization/training seeds: 43,44,45; data split held fixed.
data_split_seeds: 1 fixed split per dataset for this experiment.
attack_seeds: 0 for scalar AUC; threshold-dependent metrics use deterministic cross-fitting with a fixed fold seed.
record_bootstrap_replicates: 5000 stratified record bootstraps within each target, resampling members and non-members separately.
structural_configuration_handling: Do not pool the 42 targets as independent structural evidence. Compute per-target metrics, paired Z−ZZ differences within pair and seed, then cluster-bootstrap matched-pair IDs while retaining all seeds within each pair.
metrics: Train accuracy/loss; test accuracy/loss; generalization gap; ROC AUC; cross-fitted balanced accuracy; cross-fitted membership advantage; TPR@10% FPR primary and TPR@5% FPR secondary.
aggregation_method: Per target: metrics from raw member/non-member records. Per pair: mean±SD across 3 target seeds. Global residual encoder effect: mean paired Z−ZZ difference across pair-level seed means.
ci_95_method: Per-target AUC: stratified percentile bootstrap over records. Aggregate Z−ZZ effect: 5000-replicate cluster percentile bootstrap over matched-pair IDs, preserving all target seeds and pairing. Report seed SD separately; do not label record-bootstrap CI as seed uncertainty.
hypothesis: After verifying similar retrained train/test behavior and gap, residual Z-versus-ZZ MIA differences should be small; this supports encoder-induced, overfitting-mediated leakage rather than an independent encoder-family effect.
planned_table: Table MG-1: pair/seed train, test, gap and matching tolerances. Table MG-2: encoder-wise MIA mean±SD and paired Z−ZZ differences with cluster-bootstrap 95% CI.
planned_plot: Paired-dot plot of Z versus ZZ AUC by matched pair, with thin lines for target seeds and thick pair means; separate panel for retrained gap difference.
low_fpr_policy: Do not report TPR@0.1% or 1%. With 50 non-members, FPR resolution is 2%; with 100, it is 1%. Use 10% as primary common operating point and 5% as secondary.
estimated_runs: 42 total target trainings; 36 complete, 6 MNIST runs remain.
status_notes: Matching is not considered validated until retrained train/test metrics are extracted. Predeclare matching tolerances, e.g. |Δgap|≤0.02 primary and ≤0.05 sensitivity.

structural_scope: Use all completed predeclared high-risk and low-risk configurations from the matched target table; preserve every selected target and seed.
experimental_unit: One structural high/low comparison block, with all target seeds retained inside the block.
attack_seeds: 0 for scalar AUC; deterministic cross-fitting for threshold-dependent metrics.
record_bootstrap_replicates: 5000 per target for AUC and curve-derived metrics.
structural_configuration_handling: Aggregate first within target seed and structure. For global high−low effects, use a hierarchical bootstrap over dataset/configuration blocks and then target seeds; never treat the six attack scores or record bootstraps as independent models.
metrics: Loss AUC primary; correctness AUC; one representative confidence-family AUC; balanced accuracy; membership advantage; TPR@10% and TPR@5%.
aggregation_method: Report each dataset/encoder block and an overall high−low mean difference. Confidence, entropy, margin and maximum probability are grouped as one confidence-family result for binary tasks when their rankings are identical.
ci_95_method: Per-target stratified record bootstrap. Overall high−low contrast: 5000-replicate hierarchical percentile bootstrap over structural blocks with seeds nested. Because the number of blocks is small, also report all block-level effects and mean±SD.
hypothesis: Predeclared high-risk configurations have stronger MIA than low-risk configurations, consistent with the structural-risk proxy.
planned_table: Table HR-1: high versus low MIA metrics by dataset and encoder, with mean±SD across target seeds and aggregate paired difference.
planned_plot: Grouped point/interval plot of high- and low-risk loss AUC; show individual target seeds rather than only bars.
low_fpr_policy: TPR@10% primary; TPR@5% secondary; suppress 0.1% and 1%.
estimated_runs: No extra runs beyond completion of E1.
status_notes: This is supportive evidence, not a causal test of encoder family independent of the gap.

experiment: Pre-specified multi-seed feature-map × repetition × depth factorial subset
structural_scope: MNIST-QNN: 3 feature maps × reps {1,5} × depth {2,6} × 3 target seeds = 36 trained targets.
experimental_unit: One independently trained target model; target seeds are nested within one of 12 structural cells.
target_model_seeds: 3 model seeds: 43,44,45 with one fixed data split.
data_split_seeds: 1 fixed split in the primary factorial.
structural_configuration_handling: Compute cell means over target seeds. Main effects are paired contrasts across matched structural cells. Cluster/hierarchical bootstrap structural cells and retain all seeds; do not count three seeds as three different structural configurations.
metrics: Train/test accuracy and loss; gap; loss AUC; confidence-family AUC; correctness AUC; balanced accuracy; membership advantage; TPR@10% and TPR@5%; parameter and gate counts.
aggregation_method: Per cell: mean±SD across 3 target seeds. Repetition effect: r5−r1 within feature-map×depth blocks. Depth effect: d6−d2 within feature-map×repetition blocks. Encoder effects: pairwise contrasts within repetition×depth blocks.
ci_95_method: 5000-replicate hierarchical percentile bootstrap: resample matched structural contrast blocks, then resample target seeds within selected blocks. Report raw block effects and seed SD because only 4–6 blocks support each contrast.
hypothesis: Repetition produces larger adverse changes in gap/test utility and MIA than depth in the controlled subset; encoder-family effects are dataset/configuration dependent rather than universal.
planned_table: Table F-1: 12 cells with mean±SD. Table F-2: paired main-effect contrasts for repetition, depth and feature-map family with bootstrap 95% CIs.
planned_plot: Interaction plots for gap and AUC versus repetitions, faceted by feature map and depth, with points for target seeds and mean±SD error bars.
low_fpr_policy: 10% primary and 5% secondary unless the non-member count is enlarged. Do not display 0.1% or 1%.
status_notes: All 36 outcomes must be reported, including failed or near-chance attacks; no outcome-based filtering.

structural_scope: 6 MNIST-QNN cells: 3 feature maps × reps {1,5} at one predeclared depth, evaluated on 3 data-split seeds.
experimental_unit: One target model trained on one independently generated/sampled data split.
target_model_seeds: 1 fixed model seed (43) to isolate split variability.
structural_configuration_handling: Pair structural comparisons within the same split seed. Do not combine this variation with target-initialization SD from E3.
metrics: Train/test accuracy and loss; gap; loss AUC; confidence-family AUC; correctness AUC; balanced accuracy; membership advantage.
aggregation_method: Per structural cell: mean±SD across split seeds. Repetition and encoder contrasts are paired within split seed.
ci_95_method: With only 3 split seeds, use mean±SD as the primary variability summary. For aggregate paired effects, use a 5000-replicate paired bootstrap over split seeds and structural blocks, labeled exploratory.
hypothesis: The direction of the principal encoder/repetition trends is not an artifact of one train/test split.
planned_table: Table S-1: split-seed target metrics and paired structural effects.
planned_plot: Slope plot showing r1→r5 changes for each split seed and encoder.
low_fpr_policy: Same common operating points as E3.
status_notes: Run only after code exposes separate data and model seeds. If not run, explicitly state that all main comparisons use a fixed split and do not estimate split variability.

structural_scope: Moons and MNIST × Z/ZZ/effSU2 × reps {1,5} × 3 data seeds = 36 encoder-only evaluations.
experimental_unit: One encoder geometry computed on one dataset realization/split; no target training.
data_split_seeds: 3: 43,44,45, using the same train/test sampling rules for all encoders within each seed.
simulator_seeds: Not applicable for exact statevector geometry.
record_bootstrap_replicates: Optional 2000 record-pair bootstraps within each geometry run for similarity metrics; this is secondary to data-seed variability.
structural_configuration_handling: Keep encoder/repetition comparisons paired within dataset seed. Add class-similarity gap = within-class similarity − between-class similarity.
metrics: Train–train, train–test and test–test similarity; class-similarity gap; MMD²; centered kernel-label alignment; effective rank.
aggregation_method: Per dataset×encoder×repetition cell: mean±SD across 3 data seeds. Repetition effect: r5−r1 paired within dataset×encoder×seed.
ci_95_method: Primary display: mean±SD across data seeds. Aggregate repetition effects: 5000-replicate paired/hierarchical percentile bootstrap over dataset×encoder blocks with data seeds nested. Per-cell bootstrap CI across only 3 seeds must be labeled exploratory, not definitive.
hypothesis: Increasing repetitions raises effective rank and reduces class-aligned geometry, while train/test MMD remains near zero; this supports the encoder→geometry→generalization pathway rather than direct pre-training membership separation.
planned_table: Table G-1: geometry mean±SD by dataset, encoder and reps. Table G-2: paired r5−r1 effects with bootstrap CIs.
planned_plot: Three separate figures: effective rank, kernel-label alignment, and class-similarity gap versus repetitions, with individual seed points and mean±SD.
estimated_runs: 36 encoder-only evaluations; 12 already exist for one seed, so 24 new evaluations if seed 43 is reproducible.
status_notes: Geometry uncertainty captures dataset sampling/split variation, not target-model training stochasticity.

structural_scope: Three predeclared saved target checkpoints representing low-, medium- and high-risk configurations; same samples and checkpoints under exact, ideal finite-shot, and backend-noisy finite-shot conditions.
experimental_unit: One simulator seed applied to one fixed target checkpoint, shot count and execution mode. The target checkpoint is held fixed; simulator replicates are not target-model replicates.
target_model_seeds: 1 fixed target-model checkpoint per risk regime, preferably the same predeclared target seed (43) for all three.
data_split_seeds: Fixed to the checkpoint's original split.
simulator_seeds: 10 paired seeds per shot count and mode.
record_bootstrap_replicates: Store 2000 stratified record-bootstrap CIs per simulator replicate if computationally convenient; primary noisy error bars are across simulator seeds.
structural_configuration_handling: Analyze each target separately. Pair ideal-shot and noisy-shot outputs by simulator seed and shot count. Do not generalize these three checkpoints to all architectures/backends.
metrics: Target train/test accuracy and loss; gap; loss AUC; confidence-family AUC; correctness AUC; cross-fitted balanced accuracy; membership advantage; TPR@10% and TPR@5%; changes from exact and ideal-shot baselines; transpiled depth/gate counts.
aggregation_method: For each target×mode×shot: mean±SD across 10 simulator seeds. For noisy−ideal and finite-shot−exact changes: paired mean differences by simulator seed.
ci_95_method: 5000-replicate paired percentile bootstrap over the 10 simulator seeds for mode/shot differences. Keep any per-run record-bootstrap CI in separate columns. Do not combine simulator and target-model uncertainty into one unlabeled interval.
hypothesis: The structural ordering is not completely erased by finite shots/backend-derived noise, although utility and absolute MIA strength may change.
planned_table: Table N-1: exact, ideal-shot and noisy-shot utility/MIA mean±SD. Table N-2: paired degradation or change from ideal-shot with 95% CI.
planned_plot: MIA AUC versus shots and target accuracy versus shots, one figure each, with exact horizontal reference and mean±SD over simulator seeds.
low_fpr_policy: With 100 non-members, 1% corresponds to one false positive and is too unstable. Use 10% primary and 5% secondary.
estimated_runs: 3 targets × 2 shot-based modes × 3 shot levels × 10 simulator seeds = 180 Aer evaluations, plus 3 exact baselines.
status_notes: Require explicit noise-load success. An ideal fallback must be marked failed for the noisy condition. This is a noisy finite-shot sanity check, not hardware execution.

experiment: Controlled architecture-wrapper comparison and resource accounting
structural_scope: 3 predeclared structural configurations × QNN/HQNN/QCNN/MLP-QNN × 3 target seeds = 36 targets under a common protocol.
experimental_unit: One independently trained architecture wrapper; architectures are paired within structural configuration and target seed.
structural_configuration_handling: Compare wrappers only within the same structure×seed block. Report total, classical and quantum trainable parameters and transpiled/native gate counts.
metrics: Train/test accuracy and loss; gap; loss AUC; confidence-family AUC; correctness AUC; balanced accuracy; membership advantage; parameter counts; gate counts; runtime.
aggregation_method: Per wrapper×structure: mean±SD across target seeds. Global wrapper contrasts: paired differences within structure×seed.
ci_95_method: 5000-replicate hierarchical paired bootstrap over structural configurations and seeds. With only three structures, show all structure-specific results and treat aggregate CIs as exploratory.
hypothesis: Complete wrappers differ in utility and leakage, but differences cannot be attributed solely to the quantum architecture; parameter/preprocessor/head information explains the comparison scope.
planned_table: Table A-1: wrapper metrics and resources by structure. Table A-2: paired wrapper contrasts versus QNN.
planned_plot: Paired architecture comparison for gap and AUC with one line per structure×seed; separate parameter/gate-count plot.
status_notes: Use 'complete-wrapper comparison', not a pure causal quantum-architecture claim.

experiment: AUC–generalization relationship and residual structural regression
structural_scope: Primary inference uses the complete 36-target pre-specified factorial subset; matched targets are analyzed separately and not merged as if randomly sampled.
experimental_unit: One target model, with 3 target seeds nested within each of 12 structural cells.
data_split_seeds: 1 fixed split in the primary model.
record_bootstrap_replicates: Per-target AUC CIs already handled; regression uncertainty is over structural cells.
structural_configuration_handling: Cluster-bootstrap 12 structural cells, retaining all seeds. Standardize continuous predictors within the analysis set. Do not include gap together with both train and test accuracy because gap = train accuracy − test accuracy.
metrics: Loss AUC outcome; gap, train accuracy, test accuracy, feature map, reps, depth, log gate count, log trainable parameters; Spearman/Pearson association and standardized regression coefficients.
aggregation_method: Fit two predeclared models: M1 AUC ~ gap + feature-map + reps + depth. M2 AUC ~ train accuracy + test accuracy + feature-map + reps + depth + log(gates) + log(params), excluding gap to avoid exact collinearity. Report cell-mean sensitivity analysis.
ci_95_method: 5000-replicate cluster percentile bootstrap over structural cells for correlations, coefficients and R². If a bootstrap sample is rank-deficient, record and exclude it, and report the valid-replicate fraction.
hypothesis: Gap is positively associated with AUC; after conditioning on gap or train/test behavior, residual encoder coefficients are smaller and potentially uncertain, supporting a mediated interpretation.
planned_table: Table R-1: correlations and two regression specifications with standardized coefficients, CIs, R² and valid-bootstrap fraction.
planned_plot: AUC versus retrained gap with feature-map markers, target-seed points and cell mean±SD; coefficient forest plot for M1 and M2.
low_fpr_policy: AUC is the regression outcome; low-FPR TPR may be a secondary sensitivity only at 10% FPR.
estimated_runs: No extra runs beyond E3; CPU analysis.
status_notes: Inference is bounded to the pre-specified factorial subset; it is not an all-sweep causal model.

structural_scope: Run the existing learned prediction-vector attack on the same completed matched and/or factorial target payload set without outcome filtering.
experimental_unit: One independently trained attacker seed on a fixed target-output dataset. Target-model metrics remain grouped by target checkpoint.
target_model_seeds: Use all available target seeds in the chosen payload set.
record_bootstrap_replicates: Optional 2000 evaluation-record bootstraps per attack seed; primary attack-training uncertainty is across attacker seeds.
structural_configuration_handling: Use identical target payloads and attack train/test protocol for every attacker seed. Pair seed-level comparisons across targets.
metrics: Attack ROC AUC; balanced accuracy; membership advantage; TPR@10% and TPR@5%; calibration of attack output if available.
aggregation_method: Per target or target group: mean±SD across 5 attacker seeds. Compare learned attack with loss and confidence threshold attacks on the same records.
ci_95_method: 5000-replicate percentile bootstrap over attacker seeds for aggregate attack differences; with n=5, report raw seed values and mean±SD alongside the CI.
hypothesis: The structural ordering is not unique to a single attacker initialization or scalar score.
planned_table: Table L-1: learned-attack metrics by attacker seed and target group; comparison with threshold baselines.
planned_plot: Seed-level learned versus threshold AUC paired plot.
estimated_runs: 5 attacker trainings if the existing script trains one global attacker per seed; otherwise report per-target cost before execution.
status_notes: Do not build a full LiRA/reference-model bank for the rebuttal.

structural_scope: Existing valid sweep rows, excluding invalid historical effSU2 repetition duplicates until corrected results are available.
experimental_unit: One unique structural configuration cell. Duplicate rows and repeated seeds, when present, are grouped before attribution.
target_model_seeds: Historical sweep has one run per configuration; no target-seed uncertainty can be claimed.
structural_configuration_handling: First audit the exact original attribution method. Preserve it if valid. Resample unique structural cells, stratified by dataset/architecture, and rerun attribution. Add one prespecified sensitivity method such as partial R²/ANOVA or permutation importance.
metrics: Normalized factor contribution; partial R² or equivalent sensitivity metric; ranking stability; rank correlation between original and sensitivity methods.
aggregation_method: Report attribution by dataset/architecture and pooled only when the design supports pooling. Do not interpret configuration bootstrap as training stochasticity.
ci_95_method: 5000-replicate stratified configuration-cell percentile bootstrap. Report median contribution and 2.5/97.5 percentiles, plus factor rank frequency.
hypothesis: Encoder family, repetitions, width and their interactions remain higher-ranked than lower-level variational gate/topology factors on valid data.
planned_table: Table FA-1: attribution estimate, 95% configuration-bootstrap CI and rank frequency.
planned_plot: Contribution plot with asymmetric percentile intervals; ranking-stability heatmap or dot plot.
estimated_runs: No target retraining for valid Z/ZZ data; CPU analysis only.
status_notes: The exact method cannot be finalized until the existing attribution script is audited. Any new sensitivity method must be labeled as such rather than silently replacing the paper's method.
